title: Confusing Number II
summary: A confusing number is one that transforms into a distinct number upon a 180-degree rotation, with valid digits including 0, 1, 6, 8, and 9 becoming 0, 1, 9, 8, and 6 respectively, while 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7 become invalid.
statement: A confusing number is one that transforms into a distinct number upon a 180-degree rotation, with valid digits including 0, 1, 6, 8, and 9 becoming 0, 1, 9, 8, and 6 respectively, while 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7 become invalid. After rotation, leading zeros are disregarded. For instance, rotating 8000 results in 0008, which is simply 8. Given an integer n, count the confusing numbers within the range [1, n].
constraints: Count positive confusing numbers at most n.
Only digits 0,1,6,8,9 remain valid after rotation.
hints: Generate only numbers composed of rotatable digits.
Carry both the forward number and its rotated value while appending digits.
Count a nonzero value when it is within n and differs from its rotation.
The DFS enumerates each valid-digit integer once and prunes every prefix exceeding n.
editorial: The DFS enumerates each valid-digit integer once and prunes every prefix exceeding n.
